summary: SRanger implemented as one controller (SRangerController) with modes MOVING (initial), TURNING, FINAL; a Sensor (distance), a Clock (now), an Actuator (apply/lastCommand), sealed InputEvent {Obstacle, Tick, EndTask} and OutputEvent {Move(lv, av)}, and SRangerConstants {MOVE_VEL, TURN_VEL, OBSTACLE_THRESHOLD, TURN_DURATION}. All 23 requirements are traced in result_codegen.json. SR-DC1 holds structurally: the initial mode plus six step() branches give seven transitions, one per SR-Beh requirement, with no repeated (source mode, trigger) pair. Eight items are flagged below: two invented defaults, four design choices, one model-fidelity note on a fractional constant, and one scope note on ignored events.

issues.title: Sensor: value of the 'large default' distance and handling of invalid readings
issues.raw: SR-DM5 requires distance() to return 'a large default value' when no reading is available but does not give the value. Chosen: NO_READING_DISTANCE = 1000.0 m (far above OBSTACLE_THRESHOLD = 0.5 m). A negative or NaN measurement passed to update() is also treated as 'no reading' and stored as 1000.0, which keeps distance() non-negative as SR-DM5/SR-SF1 require.
issues.fix_directive: Confirm 1000.0 m is acceptable as the no-reading distance, or supply the intended value; change NO_READING_DISTANCE in Sensor.java.

issues.title: Actuator: stored command before any command is issued
issues.raw: SR-DM6 says the actuator stores the latest issued command but not what it holds before the first one. Chosen: Move(0.0, 0.0) (stopped). In practice the controller constructor issues Move(MOVE_VEL, 0.0) immediately, so this value is only observable before the controller exists.
issues.fix_directive: None needed unless a different pre-command state is wanted.

issues.title: Moving -> Turning uses both the obstacle event and the obstacleDetected guard
issues.raw: SR-Beh2 triggers Moving -> Turning on the obstacle event; SR-GP1 says obstacleDetected (distance <= obstacleThreshold) is the guard on that transition. Both are combined: trigger Obstacle, condition obstacleDetected. An obstacle event that arrives while distance() > OBSTACLE_THRESHOLD (e.g. a stale event) is ignored and the robot stays in Moving, consistent with 'remains in Moving as long as the IR distance reading is above the threshold'.
issues.fix_directive: If the transition should fire on the event alone, drop '&& obstacleDetected' from the Moving branch (SR-GP1 would then be unused).

issues.title: Turning: priority endTask > timed exit > tick; tick self-loop conjoins !turnDurationElapsed
issues.raw: The requirements give no explicit priority between the autonomous Turning -> Moving transition (SR-Beh5) and the tick self-loop (SR-Beh7). Since tick arrives every control cycle, placing the tick self-loop first would starve the timed exit. Order chosen: EndTask (operator shutdown, SR-Beh6) first, then turnDurationElapsed, then Tick && !turnDurationElapsed (the negation is required by the profile because the branch sits below a predicate-only branch). In the model the two are therefore mutually exclusive.
issues.fix_directive: None expected; revisit only if the timed exit should yield to tick.

issues.title: Power-up entry action of Moving is issued from the constructor
issues.raw: SR-FR1 says Move(moveVel, 0) is issued on entering Moving, and SR-Beh1 makes Moving the power-up mode. step() only performs transitions, so the power-up entry is performed in the SRangerController constructor (actuator.apply(new OutputEvent.Move(MOVE_VEL, 0.0))). Without it the robot would sit in Moving with no forward command until the first Turning -> Moving.
issues.fix_directive: If the extractor or profile checker objects to an actuator call in the constructor, move the power-up command to the platform start-up instead and note SR-FR1 as partially covered.

issues.title: Time source: Clock class and clock-reset ordering
issues.raw: SR-Var1/SR-FR2 need 'the current time' but name no time source. A Clock class with now() (monotonic seconds since construction, from System.nanoTime) is introduced; clockResetTime = clock.now() on entering Turning and turnDurationElapsed = clock.now() - clockResetTime >= TURN_DURATION, which the extractor maps to a RoboChart clock and since(clockResetTime). On the Moving -> Turning branch the clock is reset before Move(0, turnVel) is issued, so the turn duration is measured from the moment of the transition.

issues.title: OBSTACLE_THRESHOLD = 0.5 is rounded up to 1 in the model's constants interface
issues.raw: Per the profile, a fractional constant is rounded up to the next integer in the extracted constants interface. OBSTACLE_THRESHOLD = 0.5 m is the only fractional constant (MOVE_VEL 1.0, TURN_VEL 2.0, TURN_DURATION 2.0 are integral). Its exact value matters to the obstacleDetected guard: the Java tests distance <= 0.5, the model will test distance <= 1. Because distance() is an uninterpreted function in the model, deadlock/divergence results are unaffected, but the model guard is weaker than the Java guard.
issues.fix_directive: No Java change proposed (rescaling the unit would contradict SR-DM2's metres). Treat the model's threshold value as approximate when reading verification results.

issues.title: Events without a transition are ignored; Final is terminal
issues.raw: No requirement defines obstacle in Turning, or any event in Final. These events are ignored (no transition, no action). Final has an empty mode block and no outgoing transitions (SR-FR3 'terminal'); no extra transitions were invented, keeping SR-DC1's one-transition-per-SR-Beh mapping exact.
issues.fix_directive: None expected; a verifier that requires an enabled operation in Final would need a requirement for it.
